reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) discusses wear resistance and hardness in Ni-based alloys and AlCoCrFeNi/WC composites, none of which address the key premises about lightweight HEAs, lattice distortion, oxide formation, or the effect of light element content on phase stability and corrosion/oxidation resistance.
premises: High fractions of light elements (Al, Ti) can form a uniform, disordered nanostructure with severe lattice distortion in lightweight HEAs.
Severe lattice distortion promotes in situ formation of a stable, passivating Al2O3-rich oxide layer at high temperatures.
This dual effect improves specific strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Exceeding an optimal light element content causes phase separation or brittle intermetallic formation, losing beneficial effects.
